newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks ends touch higher after quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: French stocks ends touch higher after quiet trade.

text.p: French shares managed to finish in positive ground after spending much of the day in loss. Traders said the market was drifting and heavily influenced by U.S. market activity on the eve of the presidential election.
"It's very quiet," one trader said. However, the Dow shaded higher, which gave some slight impetus to Paris.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 1.64 points or 0.08 percent at 2,142.15 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,147 from 2,142 on Thursday's close. The market was closed on Friday for a public holiday.
* Lagardere clawed back much of its earlier losses, ending down 0.62 percent at 160.50 francs after shedding more than three percent earlier in the session.

Traders said newspaper reports of potential legal challenges to its Thomson offer and the placing of chairman Jean-Luc Lagardere under investigation in an alleged fraud case sparked short-term selling

* UAP up 1.69 percent at 108 francs, on renewed speculation of an acquisition by Axa, prompted by an short article in last Thursday's Nouvel Observateur. Axa was off 0.06 percent at 319.10 francs. UAP again denied the rumours.

* Castorama rose 18 francs to 893, helped by a report in British Oberver Sunday newspaper which said Kingfisher Plc was looking to extend its home improvements interests in France. The British retailer could take a minority stake in Castorama or Leroy Merlin, part of the Auchan group, it said.
A Castorama spokeswoman said it was not surprising Kingfisher wanted to expand outside Britain but declined to comment further.
* A Leroy Merlin spokesman said he had not heard of Kingfisher's reported intentions but believed the biggest firms want to consolidate their market share through mergers.
* Cerus firms 3.94 percent at 137.10 francs. Traders said the market believes the conditions were right for CGIP to buy Cerus's stake in Valeo.
Valeo was up 1.3 percent at 310.88 francs.
* Euro Disney gained 2.49 percent to 10.30 francs, after losing heavily last week
* Club Med continues to lose grounf, down 2.17 percent at 314.90 francs
* Peugeot up 0.19 percent at 534 francs, Renault up 2.27 percent at 112.80 after October figures showed new car sales rose 24.7 percent.
